title: Cube Reconstruction / lines / view
description: Fold the six exterior faces and compare the printed markings.

difficulty.label: Uncalibrated
difficulty.basis: Track an ordered corner and transport the orientation of individual motifs.

question: The net is shown from the printed side. Place that side down before folding upward, so the markings face outward. The left image is the net of a small cube, with its six faces having different patterns. The net is folded upwards to form the cube. Which of the following adjacent pattern combinations is possible when viewing the cube from an isometric perspective? Please choose from options A, B, C, or D.

annotation.Question: The left image is the net of a small cube, with its six faces having different patterns. The net is folded upwards to form the cube. Which of the following adjacent pattern combinations is possible when viewing the cube from an isometric perspective? Please choose from options A, B, C, or D.

Explanation.C: Assuming the base is the square in the 2nd row, 1st column of the net, and the right face is the square to its right. Option C is correct because it shows the Front-Top-Left view.
Explanation.D: Assuming the base is the square in the 2nd row, 1st column of the net, and the right face is the square to its right. Option D is incorrect because the face with the non-centrosymmetric pattern has been rotated.
Explanation.B: Assuming the base is the square in the 2nd row, 1st column of the net, and the right face is the one to the right of the base. Option B is incorrect because it is the Back-Top-Right view mirrored horizontally.
Explanation.A: Assuming the base is the square in the 2nd row, 1st column of the net, and the right face is the one to the right of the base. Option A is incorrect because it is the Front-Top-Right view mirrored horizontally.

answer.explanation: Reading the net from its upper left, the top, left and right faces come from diagonal (column 4, row 2 from the upper left), then cross (column 1, row 1 from the upper left), then parallel (column 5, row 2 from the upper left). All three markings retain the pictured orientation.

options.label: A
options.explanation: The three faces meet, but tee (column 2, row 1 from the upper left), fork (column 3, row 1 from the upper left), ring (column 3, row 2 from the upper left) in top/left/right order reverses their order around the vertex.

options.label: B
options.explanation: The three faces meet, but diagonal (column 4, row 2 from the upper left), ring (column 3, row 2 from the upper left), fork (column 3, row 1 from the upper left) in top/left/right order reverses their order around the vertex.

options.label: C
options.explanation: Reading the net from its upper left, the top, left and right faces come from diagonal (column 4, row 2 from the upper left), then cross (column 1, row 1 from the upper left), then parallel (column 5, row 2 from the upper left). All three markings retain the pictured orientation.

options.label: D
options.explanation: The face order matches. The right face from tee (column 2, row 1 from the upper left) would need an extra 90 degree counterclockwise turn to reproduce the view.
